observation_summary: The application throws an OutOfMemoryError when processing a large number of data points because it attempts to instantiate a full N x N matrix for weights, even when the weights are diagonal (uncorrelated).
hypothesis: The root cause is an inefficient algorithmic choice in the Weight class constructor and the squareRoot method of AbstractLeastSquaresOptimizer. Instead of using a sparse representation (DiagonalMatrix) for uncorrelated weights, the code forces the creation of a dense N x N matrix, leading to memory exhaustion for large N.
prediction: The fix will involve replacing the dense matrix instantiation in the Weight constructor with a DiagonalMatrix and updating the squareRoot method to handle DiagonalMatrix efficiently without performing full EigenDecomposition.
experiment_rationale: The provided fix diff confirms that the Weight constructor was changed to use a new DiagonalMatrix class instead of creating a full matrix via MatrixUtils.createRealMatrix, and the squareRoot method was updated to handle DiagonalMatrix as a special case, confirming the algorithmic inefficiency was the root cause.
reasoning_summary: The defect is an efficiency problem in the computational strategy used to represent and process weight matrices. The original implementation used a dense matrix representation for what is effectively a diagonal (sparse) data structure, causing memory exhaustion. This is a classic algorithmic/method-level correction where the procedure for handling data was optimized to avoid unnecessary memory allocation.
evidence_used: The bug report states: 'When using the Weigth class to pass a large number of weights to multivariate vector optimizers, an nxn full matrix is created... This exhausts memory when n is large.'
The fix diff shows the Weight constructor being changed from creating a full matrix to using a 'DiagonalMatrix'.
The fix diff shows the squareRoot method being updated to handle 'DiagonalMatrix' specifically, avoiding the expensive EigenDecomposition.

alternative_types.why_not_primary: While a new class (DiagonalMatrix) was introduced, the root cause is the inefficient algorithmic implementation of the weight handling logic, not a missing design capability.
